correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, all three generators have gcd one: adjacent pair gcds divide two and the outer pair gcd divides 35. Minimality is proved for n=3,4 and n>=6; n=2,5 reduce to explicit two-generated cases. The published three-generator Herzog/Rosales gluing characterization is applied exhaustively. For n>=71, adjacent pairs cannot satisfy the required representation by strict scale inequalities; the outer pair would force s=d and (2y-d)(6n+5)=-3d with d odd dividing 35, impossible. For all remaining n=3..70 excluding 5, verify.py checks each pair and every allowable representation coefficient; only n=3,40 survive. Independently an exact Dijkstra Apéry computation gives 2g=F+1 only at 2,3,5,40 and exceptional F=43,133,1699,258529. The finite calculation and infinite proof have disjoint, explicitly exhaustive ranges.

originality.rationale: The closest source for identical objects, OEIS A069757 (public since 2003-05-16), lists Frobenius numbers but no genus/symmetry/CI classification. The full García-Sánchez–Viola text contains the structural three-generator gluing theorem but no pentagonal specialization. The full Lepilov–O’Rourke–Swanson source establishes polynomial Frobenius formulas for consecutive squares and cubes, not this quadratic pentagonal family. Fel treats integer powers, not ordinary pentagonal values. Multiple actual semantic searches for exact object, aliases, Gorenstein equivalence, numerical set {2,3,5,40}, OEIS identifier, and gcd-35 gluing returned no matching or stronger claim. Natural classifications are not considered distinct merely by terminology; here no inspected source supplies the arithmetic exclusion or exceptional index 40.

value.rationale: A069757 identifies the precise natural triple as a longstanding Frobenius object; the symmetric cases determine exactly when its monomial curve has a complete-intersection defining ideal. The isolated, genuinely 3-generated index 40 with gcd35 and the proof that no further indices occur are structural arithmetic content, not a table lookup or arbitrary cutoff. A finite exhaustive interval follows a nontrivial sharp growth obstruction derived from differences of pentagonal numbers. These cases inform the structural classification of natural figurate numerical semigroups without claiming a general formula for F.
